objectives: To obtain an updated view of the available prognostic models for heart failure patients; specifically, to review multivariable regression and machine learning models predicting heart failure progression and, when enough studies were available, quantitatively synthesize predictive performance and identify sources of heterogeneity across mortality, hospitalization, and composite outcomes.
inclusion_criteria: Population: adult human subjects with heart failure, without a defined ethnicity; each primary study's adult-age definition and heart-failure definition were accepted. Index model: multivariable regression models and machine learning techniques for predicting heart failure progression on the basis of demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical prognostic factors, including studies that developed new multivariable prognostic models and studies that performed external validation of existing models. Outcome: predictive performance for overall mortality, HF-related and all-cause hospitalizations, emergency department access, and stroke as a major adverse cardiovascular event within 5 years of inclusion; all performance measures were eligible for the systematic review, but meta-analysis was feasible only for the C-statistic. Timing: 1 to 5 years. Setting: prediction models intended to be used by healthcare professionals at any time during heart failure progression. Eligible designs included cohort and case-control studies and observational studies incorporating cohorts from randomized controlled trials. Non-English articles were eligible, and abstracts/proceedings were evaluated for inclusion.
exclusion_criteria: Cross-sectional studies were excluded. Letters and commentaries were not included in the review, although they could be used as supporting material for the primary studies. Full-text exclusions shown in the PRISMA flow were wrong population, no multivariable predictive model/insufficient model detail, wrong endpoint, wrong timing, full-text on the same cohort and same endpoint as another included study, and primary summary statistics not presented.
pmid_query: (Heart Failure OR Cardiac Failure OR Congestive Heart Failure OR HF) AND (PREDICTION OR PREDICTIVE OR PROGNOSTIC OR PROGNOSIS) AND (MODELS OR Machine Learning OR Regression Analysis OR regression OR Proportional Hazards Models) AND (Disease Progression OR evolution); Filters: from 2012-2023.
selection_evidence: The main manuscript states that 44 eligible studies are reported in Table 1. Supplementary file 3 contains a 44-study risk-of-bias table with unique study references matching the review population. The publisher RIS export preserves the reference order, and entries 28-71 correspond to these 44 included studies.
notes: Rebuilt from the supplementary RIS export and the supplementary study-reference table to restore the full 44-study review set. The prior local structuring had collapsed this paper to the 5-study SHFM meta-analysis subset.
